about: The month and day a term starts after its election where the office's own start rule is not carried on the office (federal offices carry theirs: January 20, January 3). Read by src/core2/elections-calendar.ts termStartAfter. Rows are keyed by state and office family: statewideExecutive is the governor's clause (the mayor's for D.C.) and stands for every statewide office until another clause is read; stateLegislative is the day members elected at the general election take their seats. Each row carries either a fixed `monthDay` or a `rule` (the nth weekday of a month, plus offsetDays; the first such day after the election is the start). Rows read on 2026-10-23 carry the URL of the text they quote, most from 50constitutions.org (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative). The default stands in for county and municipal offices with no county calendar row (SG-GOV-term-end-estimate, still open for them).

default.estimatedFrom: Most state and local terms begin in early January after the November election (state constitutions and charters); the exact day varies by state and is not yet read.

townOffNovember.estimatedFrom: A city or township office elected outside November takes its seat a few weeks after the vote, at the body's first regular meeting after the canvass, not on the next January 1 (municipal charters set it town by town; none is read yet). Golden-path playthrough, Oct 28, 2026: a council seat won in Gilbert, West Virginia on April 1 started on January 1, 2026, nine months later; the owner ruled every winner taking office on January 1 a defect (Oct 14).

statewideExecutive.excerpt: First Monday in December following the election.

stateLegislative.citation: AS 24.05.080 (Alaska Const. art. II, sec. 3 allows a law to set the day)
stateLegislative.excerpt: Sec. 24.05.080. Terms. The term of each member of the legislature begins on the third Tuesday in January. The term of representatives is two years, and the term of senators, four years.
stateLegislative.note: The constitution (https://50constitutions.org/ak/constitution/section-id-44573) says: "Their terms begin on the fourth Monday of the January following election unless otherwise provided by law." The statute is that law; AS 24.05.090 also convenes the legislature on the third Tuesday in January.

statewideExecutive.citation: Ark. Const. art. 6, sec. 3 and art. 5, sec. 5(b); 2019 and 2023 inaugurations
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: ...directed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives; who shall, during the first week of the session, open and publish the votes cast and given for each of the respective officers hereinbefore mentioned, in the presence of both houses of the General Assembly. The person having the highest number of votes, for each of the respective offices, shall be declared duly elected thereto
statewideExecutive.estimatedFrom: No clause fixes the day. The session opens "on the second Monday in January of each odd-numbered year" (art. 5, sec. 5(b), https://50constitutions.org/ar/constitution/section-id-60591), and the votes are published during its first week. The swearing-in "takes place Tuesday, January 10th" (2023, https://gcdd.arkansas.gov/events/governor-sanders-swearing-in-inaugural-address), and Hutchinson was "inaugurated at the state Capitol on Tuesday" in an article dated January 15, 2019 (https://katv.com/news/local/arkansas-governor-to-be-sworn-in-for-2nd-term). Both dates are the Tuesday after the second Monday in January. The Arkansas Code text was not read.

stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: No clause names the start day outright. The two-year terms count from the first Monday in January 1913, which gives the first Monday in January. A.R.S. 41-1101 (https://www.azleg.gov/ars/41/01101.htm) has members take the oath when the legislature assembles "at twelve o'clock noon on the second Monday of January each year"; if the oath day is the one that matters, use {1,2,1,0}.

statewideExecutive.citation: Ga. Const. art. V, sec. I, para. II and art. III, sec. IV, para. I

stateLegislative.citation: Iowa Const. art. III, sec. 3 (House); Iowa Code 39.8 (Senate)
stateLegislative.excerpt: ...and their term of office shall commence on the first day of January next after their election, and continue two years, and until their successors are elected and qualified.
stateLegislative.note: Representatives start January 1. Senators fall under Iowa Code 39.8 (https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/39.8.pdf): "The term of office of all officers chosen at a general election for a full term shall commence on the first day of January following the election which is not a Sunday or legal holiday". January 1 is a holiday, so senators start January 2, or January 3 when January 2 is a Sunday. One row cannot hold both, so this row uses the House date.

statewideExecutive.citation: N.H. Const. pt. 2, art. 42; 1993 and 2025 inaugurations
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: ...and the secretary shall lay the same before the senate and house of representatives, on the first Wednesday following the first Tuesday of January to be by them examined, and in case of an election by a plurality of votes through the state, the choice shall be by them declared and published.
statewideExecutive.estimatedFrom: The constitution sets the canvass day, not the oath day. "Steve Merrill's term as governor did not begin until January 7 in accordance to the Constitution of New Hampshire" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_D._Hough): January 7, 1993 was the Thursday after the first Tuesday, the first Tuesday plus 2. A search snippet (not read in full) gave Ayotte's start as January 9, 2025, the same weekday. If the canvass day itself is the start, use {1,1,2,1}. The RSA text was not found.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The senate and house shall assemble biennially on the first Wednesday of December for organizational purposes in even numbered years, ... and shall dissolve and be dissolved at 12:01 A.M. on the first Wednesday of December in even numbered years
stateLegislative.note: The old General Court is dissolved, and the new one assembles, on the first Wednesday of December. Pt. 2, art. 33 summons members for "a due meeting of senators and representatives on the first Wednesday of December, biennially". Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.citation: N.J. Const. art. V, sec. I
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The Governor's term is four years, beginning at noon of the third Tuesday in January next following the election.

stateLegislative.citation: N.J. Const. art. IV, sec. II (Senate and General Assembly terms)
stateLegislative.excerpt: Two members of the General Assembly shall be elected by the legally qualified voters of each Assembly district for terms beginning at noon of the second Tuesday in January next following their election and ending at noon of the second Tuesday in January two years thereafter.
stateLegislative.note: Senators (https://50constitutions.org/nj/constitution/section-id-82049): "Each senator shall be elected for a term beginning at noon of the second Tuesday in January next following his election". Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.citation: N.M. Const. art. V, sec. 1 and art. XX, sec. 3(A)
statewideExecutive.excerpt: ...lieutenant governor, secretary of state, state auditor, state treasurer, attorney general and commissioner of public lands, who shall, unless otherwise provided in the constitution of New Mexico, be elected for terms of four years beginning on the first day of January next after their election.
statewideExecutive.note: Art. XX, sec. 3(A) (https://50constitutions.org/nm/constitution/section-amendment-id-63228): "The term of office of every state, county or district officer, except those elected to fill vacancies, shall commence on the first day of January next after the officer's election."

stateLegislative.citation: N.M. Const. art. IV, sec. 4 and art. XX, sec. 3(A)
stateLegislative.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: Such legislative appointments as provided in this section shall be for a term ending on December 31, subsequent to the next succeeding general election.
stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: No clause names the legislators' start day. An appointed seat ends on December 31 after the next election, so the elected member starts January 1. Art. XX, sec. 3(A) starts "every state, county or district officer" on January 1, if legislators count as state officers.

statewideExecutive.citation: NRS 223.020(2) and 223.030 (Nev. Const. art. 5, sec. 2: "from the time of his installation")
statewideExecutive.excerpt: NRS 223.030 Oath. The Governor shall take and subscribe to the official oath before the Chief Justice or one of the associate justices of the Supreme Court on the 1st Monday of January next succeeding his or her election.
statewideExecutive.note: NRS 223.020(2): the Governor "shall hold office for the term of 4 years from the time of his or her installment". The installation is the oath day. Matches the earlier estimate.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The members of the Assembly shall be chosen biennially by the qualified electors of their respective districts, on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November and their term of Office shall be two years from the day next after their election.
stateLegislative.note: Senators (https://50constitutions.org/nv/constitution/section-amendment-id-142053): "their term of Office shall be four years from the day next after their election." The game's day-after-election rule {11,1,1,2}.

statewideExecutive.citation: N.Y. Public Officers Law sec. 4(1) (N.Y. Const. art. IV, sec. 1 sets no day)
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The term of office of an elective officer, unless elected to fill a vacancy then existing, shall commence on the first day of January next after his election, if the commencement thereof be not otherwise fixed by law.
statewideExecutive.note: Read through WebFetch, which returned the subdivision in three quoted segments; curl got a JavaScript challenge (HTTP 403).

stateLegislative.excerpt: The political year and legislative term shall begin on the first day of January; and the legislature shall, every year, assemble on the first Wednesday after the first Monday in January.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.citation: Ohio Rev. Code 107.01 and Ohio Const. art. III, sec. 2
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The governor's term commences on the second Monday of January next after the election.

stateLegislative.excerpt: Representatives shall be elected biennially by the electors of the respective House of Representatives districts; their term of office shall commence on the first day of January next thereafter and continue two years. Senators shall be elected by the electors of the respective Senate districts; their terms of office shall commence on the first day of January next after their election.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: The four-year term runs from the second Monday of January following the election (the Oklahoma Senate's copy of Article VI).

stateLegislative.citation: Okla. Stat. tit. 14, secs. 80.35.14 and 145 (as cited by the Oklahoma State Election Board)
stateLegislative.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: State Senate (48) Even-numbered districts 4 2026 15th day after General November 18, 2026 (f) ... State House of Representatives (101) 2 2026 15th day after General (g) ... (f) Title 14 O.S. Section 80.35.14 ... (g) Title 14 O.S. Section 145
stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: This is the State Election Board's official terms-of-office table; the statute text itself was not read. The 15th day after election day is the first Monday in November plus 16, which matches the table's November 18, 2026 and November 22, 2028.

statewideExecutive.citation: ORS 176.010; Or. Const. art. V, sec. 4; Kotek term dates
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: 176.010 Commencement of term; inauguration. The official term of the Governor shall commence upon the publication of the returns by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, as provided in section 4, Article V, Oregon Constitution
statewideExecutive.estimatedFrom: The term starts when the Speaker publishes the returns before both houses (art. V, sec. 4, https://50constitutions.org/or/constitution/section-id-88197); no statute fixes that day. Members' terms begin on the second Monday in January (art. IV, sec. 4). Wikipedia's list of governors (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Oregon) gives Kotek's start as January 9, 2023 and her term's end as January 11, 2027, both second Mondays. Matches the earlier estimate.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The tern of each Senator and Representative shall commence on the second Monday in January following his election, and shall continue for the full period of four years or two years, as the case may be, unless a different commencing day for such terms shall have been appointed by law.
stateLegislative.note: "tern" is the source's spelling. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: The Governor's term is four years, starting on the third Tuesday of January next ensuing the election (read in a constitution mirror, not an official page).

stateLegislative.excerpt: Members of the General Assembly shall be chosen at the general election every second year. Their term of service shall begin on the first day of December next after their election.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: Section 2. The Governor shall hold office for the term of four years from the second day of January of the year following his election and until his successor has been elected and qualifies.
statewideExecutive.note: English translation on Wikisource; the official text is Spanish.

stateLegislative.excerpt: Section 8. The term of office of Senators and Representatives shall begin on the second day of January immediately following the date of the general election in which they shall have been elected.
stateLegislative.note: English translation on Wikisource; the official text is Spanish.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: The governor, lieutenant governor, secretary of state, attorney general and general treasurer shall be elected on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, quadrennially commencing A.D. 1994, and every four (4) years thereafter, and shall severally hold their offices, subject to recall as provided for herein, for four (4) years from the first Tuesday of January next succeeding their election and until their successors are elected and qualified.
statewideExecutive.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The senators and representatives in the general assembly shall be elected on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, biennially in even numbered years, and shall severally hold their offices for two (2) years from the first Tuesday of January next succeeding their election and until their successors are elected and qualified.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: The term of office of the Governor shall be four years, beginning at noon on the first Wednesday following the second Tuesday in January next after his election and ending at noon on the first Wednesday following the second Tuesday in January four years later.
statewideExecutive.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The terms of office of the Senators and Representatives chosen at a general election shall begin on the Monday following such election.
stateLegislative.note: The Monday after election day is the first Monday in November plus 7. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: 3-1-2. Time of commencement of term of office. Except as otherwise expressly provided, all state, district, and county officers shall qualify and enter upon the duties of their office on the first Monday of January succeeding their election or within twenty days thereafter. However, a state officer may qualify and enter upon the duties of office on the Saturday immediately preceding the second Tuesday of January that succeeds the state officer's election.
statewideExecutive.note: Two lawful days. The Saturday option was added in 2018 (SL 2018 (SS), ch 1) and is used here; the default would be {1,1,1,0}. The Saturday before the second Tuesday is the second Tuesday minus 3. S.D. Const. art. IV, sec. 2 sets the term length only.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: Except as otherwise expressly provided, all state, district, and county officers shall qualify and enter upon the duties of their office on the first Monday of January succeeding their election or within twenty days thereafter.
stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: No legislator-specific clause was found. The legislature convenes "on the second Tuesday of January at 12 o'clock m." (S.D. Const. art. III, sec. 7, https://50constitutions.org/sd/constitution/section-id-93294); if members' terms run from that day, use {1,2,2,0}.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: The term of office of the Governor and other executive officers shall be computed from the fifteenth of January next after the election of the Governor.
statewideExecutive.note: The inauguration itself happens at the organizational session that convenes on the second Tuesday in January (art. II, sec. 8, https://50constitutions.org/tn/constitution/section-id-87068); the term is counted from January 15. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

stateLegislative.excerpt: Representatives shall hold office for two years and Senators for four years from the day of the general election
stateLegislative.note: The term runs from election day itself, which the game cannot use; the nearest rule is the day after the election, {11,1,1,2}, one day late. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.
stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: The clause fixes the term's start on election day itself (the Tuesday, 1 day after the first Monday in November), which ruleStartAfter cannot return because it takes the first start strictly after election day. The row carries the next day (offset 2), one day late; spread 0 to 1 day, the Wednesday after election day. Replaced when a term can start on the day of its election.

statewideExecutive.citation: Tex. Const. art. IV, sec. 4; session date
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: The Governor elected at the general election in 1974, and thereafter, shall be installed on the first Tuesday after the organization of the Legislature, or as soon thereafter as practicable, and shall hold his office for the term of four years, or until his successor shall be duly installed.
statewideExecutive.estimatedFrom: The constitution leaves the session date to law (art. III, sec. 5(a)). Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Legislature) says the Legislature meets "starting on the second Tuesday in January of odd-numbered years"; the Government Code 301.001 page did not load (JavaScript page). The first Tuesday after a second-Tuesday organization is the third Tuesday. Matches the earlier estimate.

stateLegislative.citation: Tex. Const. art. III, sec. 18; session date
stateLegislative.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: ...provided, however, the fact that the term of office of Senators and Representatives does not end precisely on the last day of December but extends a few days into January of the succeeding year shall be considered as de minimis
stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: Terms run a few days into January, which implies the start falls at the session's opening, "the second Tuesday in January of odd-numbered years" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Legislature). No clause naming the day was read.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: (2) Each officer shall: (a) hold office for four years beginning on the first Monday of January next after their election;
statewideExecutive.note: Matches the earlier estimate. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

stateLegislative.citation: Utah Const. art. VI, secs. 3(2) and 4(2)
stateLegislative.excerpt: (2) Their term of office shall be two years from the first day of January next after their election.
stateLegislative.note: Senators (https://50constitutions.org/ut/constitution/section-amendment-id-81788): "(2) Their term of office shall be four years from the first day of January next after their election." Art. IV, sec. 9(3) excludes legislators from the first-Monday rule. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: Saturday after the second Wednesday in January.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The members of the House of Delegates shall be elected at the general election in November 1995, and every two years thereafter for terms of two years, to begin on the second Wednesday in January succeeding their election.
stateLegislative.note: Senators (https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title24.2/chapter2/section24.2-214/): "for terms of four years, to begin on the second Wednesday in January succeeding their election." Va. Const. art. IV, secs. 2 and 3 set only the election day.

statewideExecutive.citation: 48 U.S.C. 1591 (Revised Organic Act of the Virgin Islands)
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The term of the elected Governor and Lieutenant Governor shall commence on the first Monday of January following the date of election.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The term of office of each member of the legislature shall be two years. The term of office of each member shall commence on the second Monday in January following his election

statewideExecutive.citation: Vt. Const. ch. II, sec. 49; 2025 joint resolution R-3
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: The term of office of the Governor, Lieutenant-Governor and Treasurer of the State, respectively, shall commence when they shall be chosen and qualified, and shall continue for the term of two years
statewideExecutive.estimatedFrom: The governor is "chosen" when the General Assembly counts the votes at its opening (ch. II, sec. 47) and "qualified" at the oath. The 2025 resolution (https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2026/Docs/ACTS/ACTR003/ACTR003%20As%20Adopted.pdf) reads: "That the two Houses meet in Joint Assembly on Thursday, January 9, 2025, at two o'clock in the afternoon to receive the inaugural message of the Governor." That is the Thursday after the session opens on the Wednesday after the first Monday: the first Monday plus 3. The earlier estimate {1,1,3,1} gives January 2, 2025, a week early.

stateLegislative.excerpt: The term of office of Senators and Representatives shall be two years, commencing on the first Wednesday next after the first Monday of January following their election.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.excerpt: The term shall commence on the Wednesday after the second Monday of January following their election.

stateLegislative.excerpt: Commencement of terms of office. The regular term of office of each senator and representative shall commence on the second Monday in January following the date of election.

statewideExecutive.citation: Wis. Const. art. XIII, sec. 1 (art. V, sec. 1 sets no day)
statewideExecutive.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: The political year for this state shall commence on the first Monday of January in each year, and the general election shall be held on the Tuesday next succeeding the first Monday of November in even-numbered years.
statewideExecutive.estimatedFrom: Art. V, sec. 1 says only that the governor "shall hold office for 4 years". The start is taken as the first day of the political year. The statutes could not be read: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/13/i/02 and /document/statutes/13.02 gave curl "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer" and WebFetch HTTP 503. Matches the earlier estimate.

stateLegislative.citation: Wis. Const. art. XIII, sec. 1 (art. IV, secs. 4 and 5 set no day)
stateLegislative.excerpt: The start day is not read from the text. The clause read says: The political year for this state shall commence on the first Monday of January in each year
stateLegislative.estimatedFrom: Same estimate as the governor; Wis. Stat. 13.02 (session start) could not be loaded (same errors).

statewideExecutive.citation: W. Va. Const. art. VII, sec. 1
statewideExecutive.excerpt: Their terms of office shall be four years, and shall commence on the first Monday after the second Wednesday of January next after their election.
statewideExecutive.note: The first Monday after the second Wednesday is the second Wednesday plus 5. Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

stateLegislative.citation: W. Va. Const. art. IV, sec. 7
stateLegislative.excerpt: The terms of such officers, not elected, or appointed to fill a vacancy, shall, unless herein otherwise provided, begin on the first day of January; and of the members of the Legislature, on the first day of December next succeeding their election.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.

statewideExecutive.citation: Wyo. Stat. 22-2-107 (Wyo. Const. art. 4, sec. 1 sets no day)
statewideExecutive.excerpt: 22-2-107. When elected state and county officers assume offices. All state and county officers elected at a general election shall assume their offices on the first Monday in January next following their election.
statewideExecutive.note: Matches the earlier estimate.

stateLegislative.excerpt: Members of the senate and house of representatives shall be elected on the day provided by law for the general election of a member of congress, and their term of office shall begin on the first Monday of January thereafter.
stateLegislative.note: Read in the 50constitutions.org mirror (University of Wisconsin State Democracy Research Initiative), current version as of 2026-10-23.
